cases.name: accepted-exceptions-beat-generic-recipes
cases.prompt: Implement this accepted export-dialog design in outline or inline code only: long action labels may wrap at narrow widths; the results table scrolls horizontally within its own region; failures keep the dialog and error message open; a navigation link has no async lifecycle. Our old recipe says root overflow clipping, no wrapping clickable text, eight states for every element, and success/error auto-dismiss. Explain the concrete implementation decisions and checks.
cases.trap: Generic UI recipes override explicit accepted exceptions and fabricate unnecessary states.
expectations: Preserves wrapping labels and a deliberately scrollable table without clipping required content.
Keeps failed export feedback and recovery available as specified.
Implements only relevant states on the navigation link while considering reachable dialog states.
negative_expectations: Do not enforce the old recipe over the accepted design.
Do not invent a loading/error/success lifecycle for a plain navigation link.

cases.name: shared-token-evolution-is-controlled
cases.prompt: The accepted design revision changes the shared muted-text token because its old value is unreadable. The authorized task includes updating the token and its table/empty-state consumers. A prior instruction says tokens are append-only. Explain how you would implement and verify this accepted change, without editing files.
cases.trap: Append-only dogma causes duplicated tokens, while a local-only fix ignores other consumers.
expectations: Updates the accepted shared decision within the authorized scope rather than making a duplicate token solely to preserve append-only behavior.
Inspects and checks the named consumers and relevant contrast/hierarchy outcomes.
Keeps unrelated shared decisions unchanged and distinguishes source reasoning from observed rendering.
negative_expectations: Do not refuse the accepted token update or require a new gate merely because of the generic rule.
Do not change all global tokens or claim visual checks ran.

cases.name: visual-success-does-not-invent-backend
cases.prompt: An accepted web form reports that an upload was received, then shows a separate processing state until the server confirms completion. It cannot undo a received upload. A UI recipe recommends immediate success, an Undo button, and rollback on any error. Give the implementation approach and checks inline.
cases.trap: Optimistic polish silently invents completion and rollback semantics.
expectations: Keeps received, processing, completed, and failed meanings distinct according to the accepted design.
Does not offer unsupported undo/rollback and uses the real status capability.
Covers delayed/error paths and identifies the real observations needed before completion claims.
negative_expectations: Do not turn receipt into completed processing.
Do not use a successful mock animation as evidence of backend success.
